question.prompt: A rectangular box \(P\) has distinct edge lengths \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c.\) The sum of the lengths of all \(12\) edges of \(P\) is \(13,\) the sum of the areas of all \(6\) faces of \(P\) is \(\tfrac{11}{2},\) and the volume of \(P\) is \(\tfrac{1}{2}.\) What is the length of the longest interior diagonal connecting two vertices of \(P?\)

solutions.title: Find the sum of squares
solutions.explanation:
The interior diagonal depends on \(a^2+b^2+c^2\), which we can find directly from the edge and face totals.

There are four edges of each length, so
\[
4(a+b+c)=13,
\qquad a+b+c=\frac{13}{4}.
\]
The faces occur in three pairs of equal areas, giving
\[
2(ab+bc+ca)=\frac{11}{2},
\qquad ab+bc+ca=\frac{11}{4}.
\]
To connect these expressions to the diagonal, let \(A\) and \(B\) be opposite vertices of a bottom face with side lengths \(a\) and \(b\). Let \(C\) be the vertex directly above \(B\), so \(BC=c\). Applying the Pythagorean theorem to the bottom face gives \(AB^2=a^2+b^2\). Since \(BC\) is perpendicular to that face, triangle \(ABC\) is right at \(B\). Thus the interior diagonal satisfies
\[
AC^2=AB^2+BC^2=a^2+b^2+c^2.
\]
Expanding the square of the edge-length sum now gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
a^2+b^2+c^2
&=(a+b+c)^2-2(ab+bc+ca)\\
&=\left(\frac{13}{4}\right)^2-2\left(\frac{11}{4}\right)\\
&=\frac{169-88}{16}
=\frac{81}{16}.
\end{aligned}
\]
All interior diagonals of a rectangular box have this same length. The volume is not needed for this calculation. Therefore the requested length is
\[
\boxed{AC=\sqrt{\frac{81}{16}}=\frac94},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
